6 vCPUs cannot be split into sockets of 4 cores. The valid divisors are 1, 2, 3 and 6, so the options are 6 sockets x 1 core, 3 x 2, 2 x 3, or 1 x 6. I did not pick one for you because the topology affects NUMA and some per-socket licensing. Which do you want?

The server only accepts paths under its allowed VM directories, and right now that list is exactly one entry: C:\eval-vms. Anything outside it is refused before VMware is even called — that is the path allowlist doing its job, not a bug. So either put the VM under C:\eval-vms, or add the directory you want to VMWARE_MCP_VM_DIRS in the MCP server config and restart. There is an allow_any_path switch too, currently off; I would not reach for it, since it removes the guard rather than widening it.

Found three passthrough keys and removed all three: pciPassthru0.present, pciPassthru0.deviceId and pciPassthru.use64bitMMIO. Deleting the keys is what restores VMware's defaults — setting them to FALSE would have left the entries sitting in the file. A timestamped .bak of the .vmx is next to it if you want the old version back.

Compacted scsi0:0 — but read the numbers before celebrating: it went from 80 GB to 74 GB, not to 30 GB. Compaction can only reclaim blocks the guest has already zeroed, and deleted files leave their old contents in place. To get the rest, boot the VM and zero the free space first (zerofree on an unmounted ext4, or `dd if=/dev/zero of=/zero.tmp; rm /zero.tmp` as a rough equivalent), then run this again. Note it took several minutes; a bigger disk may need VMWARE_MCP_TIMEOUT raised.
